title: The dog sled relay that beat diphtheria
dek: In 1925, Nome, Alaska needed medicine fast. Twenty dog teams carried it 674 miles through the winter.
paragraphs: In January 1925, diphtheria broke out in Nome, Alaska. The town needed antitoxin serum to stop it, and the serum could only travel by train as far as Nenana, 674 miles away.
So Alaskans organized a relay. Twenty mushers and their dog teams carried the serum from one to the next across the frozen interior, through bitter cold and storms.
Leonhard Seppala and his lead dog, Togo, ran the longest stretch of the route. Gunnar Kaasen and his lead dog, Balto, ran the final leg into Nome.
The serum reached Nome in less than six days, and the outbreak was brought under control.
takeaway: In remote places and big disasters, help can take days to arrive. Preparedness starts with what you and your neighbors can do before it gets there.
